# Intent-Driven Development

Curated by Skill Harbor: a process skill for producing useful acceptance criteria without turning specification into ceremony. When a request is ambiguous or high-impact (security, authentication, persistent data, migrations, external APIs, compliance), it inspects available context first (repo, docs, schemas, test infrastructure), exposes the genuine ambiguity, and chooses verification methods that fit the work and its risk, before or alongside implementation. It also prepares handoff artifacts for another agent or team, making complex requests testable. Explicitly not for trivial edits, one-line fixes, active debugging, code review, or requests whose acceptance conditions are already clear. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: produces documents and criteria, not code; the value depends on answering its questions honestly; overuse on trivial tasks adds ceremony for nothing. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
